translation: These few sentences suffice to exhaust its principle. If one takes up the Inner Canon (《內經》) and examines everything it says about thirst, it becomes fully clear. There are those who speak of thirst from reversal of the qi of the heart and lung; those who speak of thirst from liver bi (痹); those who speak of thirst from heat of the spleen; those who speak of thirst from heat of the kidney; those who speak of thirst from heat binding in the stomach and large intestine; those who speak of thirst from intestinal bi (腸痹); those who speak of thirst from dan-heat (癉熱) of the small intestine; those who become thirsty because of disease from malaria; those who become thirsty because of rich, sweet food and mineral drugs; those who become thirsty because of drunken satiety followed by entering the bedchamber; those who become thirsty because of distant travel, toil and fatigue, encountering great heat; those who become thirsty because of cold damage with the stomach dried; those who become thirsty because of disease-heat; those who become thirsty because of disease-wind. Although the regions of the five viscera differ, and the circumstances in which the disease is encountered each differ, their common destination is dryness (燥).
translator_notes: 五臟 rendered as 'five viscera' with 五臟 not repeated in text; 燥 kept as 'dryness' with original character.
